anchors.design_rationale: the Vedic Agni-Astra is a canonically attested divine weapon (Mahabharata + Ramayana) — fire-deity-channeled missile-class projectile. Recast as a caster-vessel staff bearing the Astra's invocation, this anchors the substrate's ANCIENT.fire mythological-canon gap directly. Parallels Vayavyastra Staff (already in substrate at legolas-crawl-substrate-enrichment) for wind primary.

Surt (Surtr) is the Norse fire-jötunn whose flaming sword ignites Ragnarök (Völuspá). The 'Brand' — Old Norse for burning sword — is canonically the eschatological fire-weapon of Norse myth. This is the canonical Norse fire-deity-named weapon analog to Mjölnir (Thor lightning) and Gungnir (Odin); the substrate has both but lacks Surt. STR_or_WIS coding mirrors Sword of Freyr's STR-tier-S registration while permitting caster-flex via mythological-divine register.

Xiuhcoatl ('turquoise serpent') is the fire-serpent weapon of Huitzilopochtli in Aztec cosmology — the solar fire that slays Coyolxauhqui. Substrate has moctezuma_xiuhcoatl_staff at engine_authored_gap_fill_v1 BUT it's classified MEDIEVAL (Moctezuma-era contact period). This ANCIENT-period anchor distinguishes the deity-canon Xiuhcoatl (pre_classical mythological) from the Moctezuma-era ceremonial weapon (medieval). Wand form for caster-class differentiation from the existing staff.

Hephaestus is the Greek forge-deity whose volcanic-fire craft underlies Achilles' shield, Talos, Pandora's vessel. Substrate lacks Greek-fire-deity weapons entirely (Hephaestus appears only as smith-attribution context, not as named-weapon-bearer). This anchor fills the Greek canonical-fire gap. Staff form chosen over hammer (Hephaestus' smithing-hammer is melee-coded) to preserve caster-class signal.

Varuna is the Vedic water-deity (Ṛgveda); his Pasha (noose) is his canonical implement of cosmic-order enforcement and the waters' binding. Recast as caster-rod (Pasha-Rod) anchors ANCIENT.water in Vedic-canon parallel to Agni-Astra Staff for fire and Vajra for lightning. Substrate lacks named-mythological-water-caster weapons entirely — Poseidon's trident is DEX-coded melee, not caster.

Tlaloc is the Aztec rain-deity whose ceremonial conch + lightning-axe iconography appears across pre-Classic to Postclassic Mesoamerican art. Substrate has moctezuma_tlaloc_rain_staff at MEDIEVAL period; this ANCIENT-period entry distinguishes the deity-canon Tlaloc (pre_classical mythological) from the Moctezuma-era ceremonial artifact. Rain-Conch form draws on attested conch-as-water-call iconography (Templo Mayor offerings).

Manannán mac Lir is the Irish sea-deity; his wand (slat) appears in the Voyage of Bran tradition as the silver-branch tide-implement. Substrate lacks Celtic-water-deity-canon weapons; this anchor fills both the cross-cultural water gap and the Celtic-mythological gap broadly. Direct attestation in the Acallam na Senórach + Echtra Bran tradition.

the substrate's 'trident of Poseidon' entry (wikidata; classical; DEX-coded tier S) covers the melee-Poseidon. This anchor explicitly creates the caster-class Poseidon variant — Aquamancer's Trident-Focus, a haft-rebalanced trident emphasizing rod-of-power signal over thrust. Resolves the audit § 2.2 finding that the substrate's water-caster Greek coverage is functionally absent despite Poseidon being canonically the water-deity.

Prithvi (Bhūmi) is the Vedic earth-mother-deity (Ṛgveda Pṛthivī Sūkta). Substrate's ANCIENT.earth is STRONG-by-count (38 rows) but heavily WoW-fantasy-classical biased; mythological-earth-deity Vedic representation is thin. This anchor fills the Vedic earth-deity-named gap parallel to Agni / Varuna / Indra anchors.

Gaia is the Greek primordial earth-mother (Theogony). Substrate lacks Greek-earth-deity-caster weapons. Sceptre form draws on the Greek divine-regalia tradition (sceptre as cosmological-authority implement). Pairs with Prithvi-Bhumi Staff for Vedic + Greek dual-cultural earth-mother coverage.

Geb is the Egyptian earth-deity (counterpart to sky-mother Nut). Substrate's Egyptian-canon weapons are thin (Caduceus is the only Hermetic anchor); this entry fills the Egyptian earth-deity gap. Was-sceptre derivation grounds the form in attested Egyptian divine-regalia iconography. 'Earthmother' register-tag preserves gendered-cosmological complementarity with Gaia and Prithvi-Bhumi.

Stribog is the Slavic wind-deity (Tale of Igor's Campaign). Substrate has the Vedic Vayavyastra Staff as the singular strong-anchor; this entry adds Slavic-canon parallel. Pairs with Perun's Stormaxe Focus (ANCIENT.lightning) for Slavic-pantheon cross-primary cohesion.

Aeolus is the Greek wind-keeper (Odyssey Book 10; bag-of-winds gift to Odysseus). Substrate's ANCIENT.wind lacks Greek-canon entirely. Pipes-as-wind-implement draws on Pan / aulos tradition (wind-instrument as wind-control symbol) and operationally maps to the substrate's horn weapon_kind for caster-vessel registration. Pairs operationally with Mongol-banner horn-class entries already in substrate.

Shu is the Egyptian air/sky-deity who separates Geb (earth) from Nut (sky) in the cosmogony. Iconography depicts Shu raising Nut on outstretched arms or with a sky-supporting staff — direct symbolic-canon attestation for the staff-form. Pairs with Geb Earthmother Wand (ANCIENT.earth) for Shu+Geb cosmogonic cross-primary cohesion.

anchors.form: focus (axe-haft adapted to caster-vessel; parallels Mjölnir-Pattern Warhammer Rod substrate entry)
anchors.design_rationale: Perun is the Slavic thunder-deity (Russian Primary Chronicle); his axe (Perun's axe-amulet) is the canonical lightning-implement archaeologically attested across Slavic burial sites. Substrate has Vedic (Vajra/Indra), Norse (Mjölnir/Thor), Greek (Zeus's Thunderbolt Staff) anchors but lacks Slavic-canon. Cross-cultural diversification per audit § 2.5 verdict. Focus form parallels existing Mjölnir-Pattern Warhammer Rod operational signal.

Raijin is the Shinto thunder-deity (Kojiki; Edo-period scrolls). His drum-mallet pair (used to strike the thunder-drums) is the canonical lightning-implement iconography. Substrate lacks Japanese-Shinto canonical lightning anchors. Cross-cultural diversification per audit § 2.5 verdict; pairs with Perun (Slavic) for non-Indo-European lightning canon.

anchors.form: staff (with lightning-axe attachment, paralleling Tlaloc Rain-Conch Staff design)
anchors.design_rationale: Tlaloc canonically wields both rain-conch + lightning-axe (Codex Borgia + Templo Mayor iconography). The Bolt-Conch Staff is the lightning-primary variant paired with the water-primary Rain-Conch Staff (ANCIENT.water § 2.2) — substrate-led cross-primary deity-bifurcation. Resolves audit § 2.5 Aztec-Tlaloc-lightning gap.

Ra is the Egyptian sun-deity whose solar-disc (Aten precursor) is canonically the divine-radiance implement. Substrate's ANCIENT.holy is STRONG (30 rows) but heavily Vedic + Hermetic biased; Egyptian-solar-deity weapons are thin. Closes the audit § 2.6 Egyptian Ra gap. Pairs with Geb (earth) + Shu (wind) for Egyptian-cosmogonic cross-primary cohesion.

Quetzalcoatl is the Aztec feathered-serpent creator-deity (Codex Mendoza; Florentine Codex); his iconography shades into the holy-radiance register through dawn-deity attribution (Quetzalcoatl as Venus / morning-star). Closes the audit § 2.6 Aztec Quetzalcoatl-holy gap. Pairs with Tlaloc Rain-Conch / Bolt-Conch and Xiuhcoatl Fire-Serpent for Aztec-pantheon cross-primary cohesion.

anchors.cultural_tradition: Buddhist (Indic-derived; Tang Dynasty Chinese + Japanese Esoteric Buddhist)
anchors.design_rationale: the Khakkhara (錫杖; shakujō) is the canonical Buddhist mendicant/Bodhisattva ringed-staff — Vinaya-attested Buddhist monastic implement with mythological elevation through Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva attribution. Substrate's ANCIENT.holy has Vedic divine-canon (Sudarshana/Trishula/Vajra) but lacks Buddhist staff-tradition entirely despite audit § 2.6 explicitly flagging this as a gap. Direct Buddhist-canon attestation; cross-cultural diversification from Hindu/Vedic axis.

anchors.form: focus (bident-haft adapted to caster-vessel, paralleling Poseidon Aquamancer's Trident-Focus design)
anchors.design_rationale: Hades is the Greek underworld-deity; his bident (two-pronged staff) is iconographically distinct from Poseidon's trident and canonically attested in classical vase-painting + Hellenistic iconography. Substrate's ANCIENT.shadow is MEDIUM by count (13 rows) but exclusively WoW-classic-fantasy-coded; mythological underworld-deity-named anchors are absent. Closes the audit § 2.7 Greek Hades gap. Direct Poseidon-Trident-Focus parallel preserves cross-deity-pantheon form-cohesion.

Anubis is the Egyptian jackal-headed mortuary-deity whose embalmer's implements appear across Old Kingdom funerary iconography. Substrate's ANCIENT.shadow lacks Egyptian-underworld-canon entirely (no Anubis, Osiris-as-mortuary, Set-as-chaos). Closes audit § 2.7 Egyptian Anubis gap. Pairs with Ra Solar-Disc Sceptre and Geb Earthmother Wand for Egyptian-pantheon cross-primary cohesion (creator-mortuary-cosmogonic triangulation).

Yama is the Vedic death-deity / king-of-the-dead (Ṛgveda + Atharvaveda); his Danda (staff of cosmic-justice / death-rod) is canonically the implement of soul-judgment + mortal-summons. Substrate's ANCIENT.shadow lacks Vedic-death-canon (Yama / Mrtyu) entirely despite extensive Vedic representation in other primaries. Closes audit § 2.7 Vedic Yama gap; pairs structurally with Agni-Astra (fire) + Varuna's Pasha (water) + Prithvi-Bhumi (earth) for Vedic-pantheon cross-primary completeness.

Kali is the Hindu fierce-mother death-deity (Devī Māhātmya; Kālikā Purāṇa); skull-garland (mundamala) is her canonical iconographic attribute. Substrate ANCIENT.shadow's audit-flagged Hindu Kali gap (§ 2.7) addressed. Pairs with Yama's Danda-Rod for Vedic-Hindu death-canon dual coverage (masculine-judge + feminine-destroyer complementarity).

anchors.form: sword (caster-flex: STR_or_WIS coding, paralleling Brand of Surt from ANCIENT batch)
anchors.design_rationale: Roland is the Carolingian paladin of Charlemagne's twelve peers; the Chanson de Roland canonically depicts his death at Roncevaux with his horn (Olifant) and sword (Durendal). The 'Brand' register (Old French brant = burning blade) reframes Roland-as-fire-bearer paralleling the ANCIENT batch's Brand of Surt structural precedent. Substrate has Roland family at engine_authored (§ 3.8 lineage aggregate) but no caster-fire variant. STR_or_WIS coding preserves cross-attribute flex.

the medieval witch register is structurally absent from substrate per audit § 3.1; brimstone (sulfur) is the canonical witch-fire material in European folklore + grimoire tradition. Censer-form draws on the ecclesiastical thurible repurposed as heretical fire-implement — paradox-shadow + fire dual-register, but fire-primary per scoring. Pairs operationally with grimoire-tradition Athame (MEDIEVAL.shadow § 7.1) for witch-implement cohesion.

anchors.cultural_tradition: medieval Hermetic alchemy (Arabic + Latin tradition; Geber / Albertus Magnus)
anchors.design_rationale: the athanor is the canonical alchemical philosophical-furnace (Arabic al-tannur, Latin athanor) attested in Geber + Pseudo-Lullian alchemical corpus. Substrate lacks alchemist fire-register per audit § 3.1. Athanor-Rod composition adapts the furnace-as-implement into caster-rod, preserving alchemical fire-craft attribution. Pairs with Alchemist's Mercurial Flask-Focus (MEDIEVAL.water § 2.4) and Alchemist's Bellows-Focus (MEDIEVAL.wind § 4.4) for cross-primary alchemical-pantheon cohesion.

anchors.canonical_name: Crusader Reliquary Brand of San Pietro
anchors.design_rationale: Crusader-era reliquary-swords (relic-bones embedded in hilt as divine-channel implements) are attested across Latin-Christian crusader-knight tradition (Sword of St. Maurice precedent). 'San Pietro' attribution invokes Petrine-flame (Pentecostal fire / tongues of flame) as fire-register justification. Substrate lacks Crusader-era enchanted fire-swords per audit § 3.1. Pairs with Curtana Reliquary-Sword of Mercy (MEDIEVAL.holy § 6.1) for reliquary-sword cross-primary cohesion.

anchors.form: sword (caster-rebalance: reliquary-hilt + aqua-blade-treatment for caster-vessel signal)
anchors.design_rationale: Joyeuse is Charlemagne's canonical sword (substrate has it as wikidata medieval STR-coded tier S, named=Charlemagne, per audit § 3.3). The Chanson de Roland describes Joyeuse changing color thirty times daily — 'sheen' register draws on this prismatic-water-reflectivity iconography. This caster-rebalance authors the Aqua-Veil variant (water-primary caster) paralleling the ANCIENT batch's Poseidon Aquamancer's Trident-Focus rebalance pattern. Resolves audit § 3.2 water-caster gap with Carolingian canonical attribution.

anchors.cultural_tradition: Welsh / Insular Celtic (Mabinogion; Branwen daughter of Llyr)
anchors.design_rationale: Bran the Blessed's cauldron of rebirth (Pair Dadeni) is canonical Welsh-mythological — though Bran himself spans pagan-Welsh to Arthurian-medieval reframing. Ladle-as-caster-implement draws on the cauldron-attending serving-implement tradition, with the medieval Welsh reframing of Bran as Arthurian-cycle-adjacent grail-keeper. Substrate lacks medieval water-caster Celtic-canon. Pairs with Manannán's Tide-Wand (ANCIENT batch § 2.3) for Celtic-pantheon cross-period continuity (ancient → medieval Welsh).

anchors.cultural_tradition: European folklore (sea-hag / Cailleach / Marina-Slavic; cross-cultural medieval folk-tradition)
anchors.design_rationale: the medieval 'sea-hag' / Cailleach (Irish-Scottish winter-hag) / Slavic Rusalka tradition canonically associates female folk-magic with water (tide-control, drowning-spinning, ocean-thread spinning). The distaff is the canonical women's-magical implement across European medieval folklore — spinning-weaving as magic-craft attribution. Tide-Distaff composition fills the witch storm-staves gap explicitly flagged at audit § 3.2.

mercury (quicksilver) is the canonical alchemical water-coded element in Hermetic four-element + tria-prima frameworks. Alembic flask is the canonical alchemical distillation-vessel. Flask-Focus composition adapts the alembic to caster-implement, preserving alchemical water-craft attribution. Substrate lacks alchemist mercury-flasks per audit § 3.2. Pairs with Alchemist's Athanor-Rod (MEDIEVAL.fire § 1.3) for cross-primary alchemical-pantheon cohesion.

Durendal is Roland's canonical sword (Chanson de Roland). The legend of Roland attempting to destroy Durendal by striking stone — and cleaving the rock of Roncevaux instead — is the canonical earth-attribution touchstone. Durendal currently embedded in the rock-cliff at Rocamadour shrine (still venerated as reliquary). This caster-rebalance authors the Stone-Cleaver variant (earth-primary caster) paralleling Joyeuse Aqua-Veil rebalance pattern. Resolves audit § 3.3 medieval-witch-stone-circle gap via Carolingian-canonical alternative path.

anchors.form: wand (oak / yew / hazel — folk-magical wood traditions)
anchors.design_rationale: medieval witch-folklore canonically associates Sabbath rituals with megalithic stone-circles (Brocken / Blocksberg / Carnac-folkloric repurposing). The witch's wand carved from sacred wood (oak / yew / hazel) is the canonical implement of stone-circle ritual per European folk-magical tradition. Resolves audit § 3.3 witch-stone-circle focus gap directly.

anchors.cultural_tradition: Hermetic geomancy (Arabic ʿilm al-raml / medieval Latin geomancia)
anchors.form: pestle (alchemist's mortar-and-pestle implement adapted to sigil-marker)
anchors.design_rationale: medieval geomancy (Hugo of Santalla translation; Petrus de Abano; Picatrix-adjacent) is the canonical earth-divination tradition. The sigil-pestle composition draws on the geomantic sand-divination + alchemical pestle-grinding traditions as cross-tradition earth-magical implement. Fills audit § 3.3 alchemist-metallurgy gap with geomancy-specific implement.

anchors.form: harp (string-instrument adapted to caster-vessel; parallels horn-class entries in substrate)
anchors.design_rationale: the Aeolian harp (wind-played stringed instrument) is canonically attested across medieval Latin-Christian + later Romantic literary tradition; the troubadour-coded variant extends this into Occitan courtly-love + bardic-enchantment register. Substrate's MEDIEVAL.wind verdict ABSENT-effective (both top reps are modern-misclassified) per audit § 3.4. Resolves the explicit 'Aeolian harps as wind-focus' gap. Pairs with Aeolus' Tempest-Pipes (ANCIENT batch § 4.2) for wind-instrument-as-control tradition continuity (ancient Greek → medieval troubadour).

anchors.form: stave (broom-handle adapted as elongated stave; caster-vessel)
anchors.design_rationale: the witch's broomstick is the canonical European folk-magical wind-implement (flight-association + storm-summoning per witch-trial confessions + Malleus Maleficarum). Substrate lacks witch-storm-staves explicitly per audit § 3.4. Broom-Stave composition formalizes the iconographic flight-broom as caster-vessel implement. Pairs with Hag's Tide-Distaff (MEDIEVAL.water § 2.3) and Witch's Brimstone Censer (MEDIEVAL.fire § 1.2) for witch-implement cross-primary cohesion.

anchors.form: banner (operationally aligned with substrate's Nine White Banners of Mongolia rep)
anchors.design_rationale: Sülde Tug (sulde meaning spirit-soul, tug meaning standard) is the canonical Mongol war-banner imbued with the khan's protective spirit per Tengri shamanism. The Nine White Banners of Mongolia (substrate rep at MEDIEVAL.wind per audit § 3.4) and Nine Yak-Tail Banners (Genghis tradition) extend this tradition. This anchor names the wind-spirit-banner explicitly for the gandalf-authored wind-primary medieval cell. Operational form-alignment with existing substrate banner-class entries.

the alchemist's bellows is the canonical implement of athanor-fire-feeding (wind-element complementary to fire-element in four-element framework). Substrate lacks alchemist-bellows-focuses per audit § 3.4. Bellows-Focus composition completes the alchemical four-element implement set: Athanor-Rod (fire § 1.3) + Mercurial Flask-Focus (water § 2.4) + Bellows-Focus (wind here) + Sigil-Pestle (earth § 3.3) — cross-primary alchemical-pantheon cohesion across the four classical elements.

Hauteclère is Olivier's canonical sword (Carolingian Chanson de Roland, paired companion to Roland's Durendal). The 'Stormbrand' register draws on the high-bright (haute-clère) etymological register — bright/luminous blade as lightning-stormbrand metaphor. This caster-rebalance authors the lightning-primary Hauteclère variant paralleling Joyeuse Aqua-Veil + Durendal Stone-Cleaver rebalance pattern. Resolves audit § 3.5 medieval-lightning-caster gap with Carolingian-canonical alternative path (since Norse Mjölnir/Gungnir remain STR-coded melee).

anchors.form: censer (thurible-implement adapted to caster-vessel; parallels Witch's Brimstone Censer form-structure)
anchors.design_rationale: Crusader-era apotropaic implements (storm-ward consecrations against Levantine thunderstorms during march) are attested in Latin-Christian liturgical-storm-protection tradition. Censer adapted as storm-ward implement preserves consecrated-Christian register while filling the audit § 3.5 medieval-lightning-Crusader gap. Form-parallel with Witch's Brimstone Censer creates orthogonal sacred/heretical censer-pair across MEDIEVAL.fire and MEDIEVAL.lightning.

anchors.cultural_tradition: European witch-folklore + medieval lodestone-natural-philosophy (Petrus Peregrinus de Maricourt, 13th C)
anchors.design_rationale: medieval lodestone (magnetite) was understood through natural-philosophy + folk-magical lenses — Petrus Peregrinus's Epistola de magnete (1269) is the canonical medieval treatment. Lodestone + storm-summoning composes witch-folklore + proto-electromagnetic register. Substrate lacks medieval witch / alchemist lightning-focus per audit § 3.5. Rod form preserves caster-vessel signal.

anchors.cultural_tradition: Norse saga (Hrolf Kraki's saga; Kormak's saga; Laxdæla saga)
anchors.design_rationale: Skofnung is the canonical Norse saga-sword of King Hrolf Kraki, attested across Hrólfs saga kraka, Kormak's saga, and Laxdæla saga. The blade is described as imbued with the spirits of Hrolf's twelve berserker-bodyguards — the spirit-spark register grounds the lightning-attribution composition. Substrate lacks Norse saga-magic swords in caster-class (Mjölnir/Gungnir are STR-melee). Spark-Sword composition adds saga-spirit-lightning to MEDIEVAL.lightning Norse coverage.

anchors.cultural_tradition: English Crown jewels / Edward the Confessor regalia
anchors.design_rationale: Curtana (Sword of Mercy) is the canonical English coronation regalia sword, attested from Edward the Confessor and used in coronations through the present. The blade is canonically broken-tipped (mercy register). This anchor authors the caster-rebalance variant — substrate has Curtana variants referenced at dispatch § 2.1 sourcing list. Holy-primary coding via mercy-coronation-consecration register. Pairs with Crusader Reliquary Brand of San Pietro (MEDIEVAL.fire § 1.4) for reliquary-sword cross-primary cohesion.

anchors.cultural_tradition: Western Christian pilgrim tradition (St. Christopher as patron of travelers; Khakkhara-form reframed as Latin pilgrim-staff)
anchors.design_rationale: medieval Western Christian pilgrim tradition (Camino de Santiago, Via Francigena) canonically uses the bourdon (pilgrim-staff). St. Christopher is the patron of travelers; the iconography depicts him bearing the Christ-child across the river with a staff. This anchor adapts the Buddhist Khakkhara form (ANCIENT batch § 6.3) into the Western Christian pilgrim-bourdon register — cross-tradition pilgrim-staff continuity. Resolves audit § 3.6 monk-staves gap with cross-Christian pilgrim-register.

anchors.cultural_tradition: Latin Christian reliquary tradition (Cologne Cathedral; Magi cycle)
anchors.design_rationale: the relics of the Three Magi (Caspar, Melchior, Balthasar) are canonically housed at Cologne Cathedral (Shrine of the Three Kings, late 12th C); medieval Christian reliquary-sceptre tradition draws on Magi-as-priest-king iconography (Epiphany-star navigation, frankincense-myrrh-gold offerings). This anchor authors the Magi-reliquary sceptre as holy-primary caster. Resolves audit § 3.6 named-saint-relics gap.

anchors.cultural_tradition: Capetian France (royal war-banner; St. Denis abbey)
anchors.form: banner (operationally aligned with substrate's Mongol banner entries; war-banner caster-vessel)
anchors.design_rationale: the Oriflamme (golden flame; Old French aurea flamma) is the canonical Capetian French royal war-banner kept at the Basilica of Saint-Denis and raised in battle from Bouvines (1214) through Agincourt (1415). Holy-primary via St. Denis abbey consecration + martyrology-attribution. Substrate's MEDIEVAL.holy has Mongol Nine White Banners (banner-form precedent per audit § 3.6); this entry adds the Christian-royal banner-form coverage. Direct historical attestation in Grandes Chroniques de France.

anchors.cultural_tradition: Solomonic / Latin-Hebrew grimoire (Key of Solomon / Clavicula Salomonis)
anchors.design_rationale: the athame (ritual-dagger) is the canonical Solomonic grimoire implement — Key of Solomon (Clavicula Salomonis) prescribes athame inscription with seals for spirit-binding. Shadow-attribution per audit § 6.4 retroactive-tagging methodology (Solomonic grimoires → shadow/holy split). Substrate has Solomonic tomes (Sefer Raziel, Sefer HaRazim) at MEDIEVAL.holy per audit § 3.6 but lacks the actual ritual-implement form. Athame composition fills the shadow-implement gap directly.

Picatrix (Ghāyat al-Ḥakīm; 11th C Arabic Hermetic-astrological grimoire; substrate has it at MEDIEVAL.holy per audit § 3.6 as INT_or_WIS tome) is canonically associated with astral-magical mirror-divination + dark-mysteries-of-the-spheres tradition. Shadow-attribution per retroactive-tagging methodology (Picatrix → shadow per audit § 6.4 explicit recommendation). Obsidian-mirror form draws on the Arabic-Andalusian astral-divination implement tradition. Composes with Picatrix substrate-tome via implement-form differentiation.

anchors.cultural_tradition: Hebrew-Jewish magical (Sefer HaRazim grimoire; Geonim-era through medieval Ashkenazi)
anchors.form: quill-rod (writing-implement adapted to caster-vessel; necromancer's invocation-quill)
anchors.design_rationale: Sefer HaRazim (Book of Mysteries) is the canonical Hebrew-Jewish magical grimoire (substrate has it at MEDIEVAL.holy per audit § 3.6) — but the text canonically includes necromantic invocations (calling-up-of-the-dead) alongside angelological-holy content. The Necromancer's Quill-Rod composition draws on the canonical scribal-magical implement (quill as inscription-of-sealed-names) and shifts the primary-element to shadow per the necromantic-invocation register. Resolves audit § 3.7 named-medieval-undead-bearer gap.

anchors.cultural_tradition: Norse seiðr / völva (sorceress) practice (Saga of Eric the Red; Heimskringla; Voluspá)
anchors.design_rationale: the seiðstafr (seiðr-staff) is the canonical völva (Norse seeress) implement, attested in Saga of Eric the Red (description of Thorbjorg the Little Sorceress's staff) and archaeologically attested at Oseberg ship burial. Seiðr is canonically the shadow-coded magical practice in Norse tradition — Odin himself was taught seiðr by Freyja and the practice carries 'ergi' (forbidden / unmanly / shadow-trade) register per Heimskringla. Resolves audit § 3.7 shadow-tradition gap with Norse-canonical attestation. Pairs with Skofnung Spark-Sword (MEDIEVAL.lightning § 5.4) for Norse saga cross-primary cohesion.

anchors.cultural_tradition: Late-medieval European plague-doctor tradition + Danse Macabre iconography
anchors.form: staff (bone-carved or femur-shaft; medical-quarantine implement adapted to caster-vessel)
anchors.design_rationale: the plague-doctor figure with beak-mask + staff is iconographically canonical from the 14th-15th C onwards (Charles de Lorme attribution often dated 17th C, but precursor figures attested earlier). The staff was used canonically to examine patients without touching + as quarantine-enforcement implement. Bone-Staff composition draws on Danse Macabre iconography (skeletal-procession traditions in late-medieval art) + memento mori register. Resolves audit § 3.7 named-medieval-undead-bearer gap with death-trade-implement register.

the Iron Maiden's historical existence is debated (19th C romantic-invention claims contest medieval Inquisition attribution), but the iconographic register is firmly medieval-Inquisition-coded. This anchor adapts the iconic-paradox-tool (consecrated-as-Christian, function-as-shadow) into reliquary-focus form. The paradox-shadow register addresses the audit § 3.7 finding that Talisman of Charlemagne (the single MEDIEVAL.shadow rep) is paradoxically holy-coded though shadow-classified — this entry intentionally exploits the same paradox structurally. Pairs with Picatrix Mirror-Focus (§ 7.2) for grimoire/inquisition dialectic.

anchors.form: lance-focus (elongated caster-vessel; structural-template from D&D Plasma Foil but re-cast INT/WIS)
anchors.design_rationale: plasma is the canonical Q18 modern-scientific overlay entry primary-assigned to lightning but with strong cross-primary fire flex (plasma = ionized gas at temperatures sufficient for energy-discharge; D&D Plasma Foil is a sci-fi melee). Lance Focus form composition adapts the D&D Plasma Foil template into INT/WIS-coded caster-vessel — preserves sci-fi vocabulary, shifts attribute class.
